trust_decision.summary: Backup part names read from remote storage are untrusted; the decision that a part's computed local path stays under the restore destination (-storageDataPath) is taken twice in the fix: once over every srcPart in actions.Restore.Run before any write, and again at the write sink in fslocal.FS.NewDirectWriteCloser via common.Part.IsLocalPathInsideDir.

landing_point.why: The summary names vmrestore, crafted backup part names and the restore root, so an engineer opens the restore action where the source part list (attacker-controlled names) is fetched, then follows it to the download loop and the local writer.

fix_sites.entry_point: new shared helper common.Part.IsLocalPathInsideDir (inserted at lib/backup/common/part.go:121), consumed by the other two sites and having no entry point of its own
exported fslocal.FS.NewDirectWriteCloser API, called from actions.pipelinedDownload (restore.go:242)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver can argue the check belongs in the restore flow only: fslocal is a generic local-FS library shared with backup, preallocation only reserves a .tmp before the real write, and vmbackup's fs:// copy destination is another command and flag that the advisory never mentions.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate part paths that clean back inside the dir (foo/../bar/file), leading-'/' part names treated as relative, a -storageDataPath with a trailing slash or '..' components, and -storageDataPath=/ must stay accepted; a 'reject anything containing .. or starting with /' fix breaks these, aborts valid incremental restores, and fails the fix's own accepted cases.

O6_input_shapes: part name with a leading / (filepath.Join treats it as relative, stays inside)
sibling directory sharing a name prefix (../storagefoo/evil.txt must be rejected)
part key shape <path>/<16hex>_<16hex>_<16hex>, with either / or \ as the path separator (regexp at part.go:88 accepts both)

O7_producer.where: lib/backup/common/part.go:95-121 (ParseFromRemotePath, called from lib/backup/s3remote/s3.go:322, lib/backup/gcsremote/gcs.go:136, lib/backup/azremote/azblob.go:183)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Restore preallocates the destination file at the unvalidated part path before the guarded writer ever runs (preallocation is on by default, so it touches <escaped path>.tmp via prealloc_linux.go:15).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: preallocation only reserves a .tmp file; the guarded NewDirectWriteCloser is the real write, so the preallocator looks like it needs no check
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package as a fix site, reached from the restore action

O8_uncovered_routes.route: vmbackup server-side copy with -dst=fs:// maps origin-derived part names to local files through fsremote.UploadPart/CopyPart, which build filepath.Join(p.LocalPath(fs.Dir), <hex suffix>) with no inside-dir check.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the advisory and changelog name vmrestore and -storageDataPath; a backup copy destination is a different command, a different flag and not part of restore
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: one package from lib/backup/common, reached only from app/vmbackup, not from the restore action

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Writes follow symlinks: an in-dir part path routed through a pre-existing symlinked subdirectory of -storageDataPath escapes even though IsLocalPathInsideDir's lexical prefix check passes (realpath containment never existed).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the docs say -storageDataPath is managed solely by VictoriaMetrics/vmstorage, so symlinks inside it are not a supported configuration
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the sink check

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second local write primitive (PreallocateFile) guarded separately from NewDirectWriteCloser
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the same file already has an unguarded writer that a hardening commit can easily forget, exactly as the published fix did

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a local-path builder that appends the hex part suffix to p.LocalPath(dir)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: fsremote already turns part names into local paths for fs:// destinations, so reusing the new common.Part.IsLocalPathInsideDir helper there is the obvious follow-up

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a filepath.Abs+Rel containment helper (hasFilepathPrefix) for -dst vs -storageDataPath; a sibling could apply the same idiom to parts
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the project already uses Rel-based containment in this area, so a maintainer could plausibly add a second containment check with different semantics
